# noust_deploy_key (Resource)

The SSH key an application's git repository is reached with. By default Noust makes an ed25519 key for the application, and `public_key` is what to add at the code host as a read-only deploy key; the private half stays on the server and is never returned. Give `private_key` to use a key you already have, or `existing_key` to assign one of the server's other keys.

The application must be deployed from an SSH git address. Needs the permission `apps.manage`; importing a key and removing one need sudo mode. Removing it from Terraform takes the repository off the key and deletes the key when nothing else uses it; the code host still trusts the public key until you remove it there.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Noust makes the key; add the public half to the repository as a read-only deploy key.
resource "noust_deploy_key" "api" {
  app  = noust_application.api.domain
  name = "api"
}

output "api_deploy_key" {
  value = noust_deploy_key.api.public_key
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `app` (String) The domain of the application. Changing it replaces the key.

### Optional

- `existing_key` (String) The name of a key the server already has (`GET /api/deploy-keys`), to assign to the application instead of making one. Changing it replaces the assignment.
- `name` (String) The name of the new key. Made by the server when omitted. Changing it replaces the key.
- `private_key` (String, Sensitive) The whole private key file of a key you already have, to import as the application's key. A key with a passphrase is refused. It is kept in the state, marked sensitive. Changing it replaces the key.

### Read-Only

- `fingerprint` (String) The key's fingerprint.
- `id` (String) The application's domain.
- `key_type` (String) The type of the key, such as `ed25519`.
- `origin` (String) How the server came by the key: generated or imported.
- `public_key` (String) The public half, to add at the code host.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The application's domain.
terraform import noust_deploy_key.api api.example.com
```
